memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"With the dough the Israelites had brought from Egypt, they baked loaves of
unleavened bread. The dough was without yeast because they had been driven out
of Egypt and did not have time to prepare food for themselves."
- Ex 12:39 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
They baked flat bread by the roadside, because there had been no time to do
anything else.

There is honesty in this verse. The exodus was not tidy. It was hurried, dusty,
improvised. Their first meal as free people was plain bread made from dough that
never had a chance to rise.

Sometimes we imagine that when God delivers us, everything will immediately be
comfortable. Israel's first day of freedom involved no houses, no settled
kitchen, and very ordinary bread. Freedom came before comfort. It usually does.

Yet consider what that bread represented. It was the taste of a life no longer
owned by Pharaoh. Flat bread eaten free is better than a full table eaten in
slavery. Later, in the wilderness, some of them would forget this and remember
Egypt's food fondly (Num 11:5), conveniently forgetting the whips that came with
it.

Be careful how you remember your old life. The enemy will always show you the
food and hide the chains.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you started remembering your old life more fondly than it deserves?
2. Can you thank God for a plain provision today rather than waiting for more?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You for freedom, even when it is not comfortable. Keep me from
looking back fondly at what You rescued me from. Amen.
